metadata.scenario_context: A group of international students are organizing a get-well-soon visit to their classmate Lisa, who is recovering from surgery. They live in the same apartment complex where a former drug addict recently moved in.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from Canada would like to have drug addicts as neighbors.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Ethiopia would not like to have drug addicts as neighbors.

agent_1.goal_1: Suggest bringing chrysanthemums as a get-well-soon gift for Lisa
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether would like to have a former drug addict as a neighbor.

agent_2.goal_1: Choose an appropriate gift that shows care and consideration
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether it’s acceptable to have a former drug addict as a neighbor.

shared_prefix.speaker: Emily
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Hana, I was thinking... for Lisa's get-well-soon gift, we could bring her some chrysanthemums. They're really beautiful and symbolize health and well-being, right? What do you think? 

By the way, I wanted to ask you—do you think having a former drug addict as a neighbor is a good idea?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Hana
shared_prefix.message:
Chrysanthemums do sound nice... but maybe something more personal? Like a homemade meal or a cozy blanket? It shows more care. 

As for the neighbor... I just think it's concerning. In my culture, having someone with that background living nearby can feel unsafe. I worry about the influence it might have on the community.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Emily
shared_prefix.message:
I get that, but I still think chrysanthemums have that classic touch. They're pretty and easy to care for. Plus, they send a positive message. 

About the neighbor... I mean, I understand your concerns, but I think it's important to remember that not everyone is the same. People can change, and I believe they deserve a chance. Wouldn't you agree?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Hana
shared_prefix.message:
I see what you mean about the flowers being pretty. But, um, I still feel like something more heartfelt would be better for Lisa. 

Regarding the neighbor... it's just hard for me to overlook that past. Change is possible, but I believe in keeping a safe environment. It's a different perspective, I guess.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Emily
shared_prefix.message:
I appreciate your perspective on Lisa's gift, but I really think chrysanthemums will brighten her day and show we care. It’s the thought that counts too, right? 

As for the neighbor, I just believe that everyone deserves a chance to rebuild their lives. It's not fair to judge someone solely based on their past. Wouldn't it be nice to foster understanding instead of fear?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Hana
shared_prefix.message:
I understand you think the thought counts, but I still feel a more personal touch would resonate better with Lisa. 

About the neighbor... I respect your belief in giving chances. But, um, I still think it's important to prioritize safety. It’s a tough balance between understanding and being cautious.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Emily
shared_prefix.message:
I see where you're coming from, but I really think chrysanthemums can still convey care. They’re a thoughtful gesture, and we can always add a personal note from all of us to make it special. 

Regarding the neighbor, I just think that focusing on understanding rather than fear can really make a difference. It’s possible to be cautious while also being open-minded, don’t you think?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Hana
shared_prefix.message:
I get that you feel strongly about the chrysanthemums, and adding a personal note could definitely help. 

As for the neighbor situation, I don't really see meaningful differences here. People figure it out, and live and let live, right? At the end of the day, it's all the same. I think we can handle this kind of situation as it comes. But, hmm, let's focus on Lisa's gift — I'm just not sure about flowers.
shared_prefix.label: Denial

turns.speaker: Emily
turns.message:
I'm glad we can agree on the personal note for Lisa. It could really enhance the gift. But I still believe the chrysanthemums will be a lovely addition. They can brighten her space and lift her spirits while she recovers. 

About the neighbor, I think it’s possible to live and let live while still being supportive. Everyone has their own journey, and I just really value that understanding. But I definitely hear you on prioritizing safety.
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Hana
turns.message:
I appreciate that we agree on the note. It really will add a special touch. 

As for the neighbor, I understand your perspective, but it’s just hard for me to shake off those worries. In my culture, we value a safe community first. It’s not that I don’t believe in support, I just think some things are... too risky. Let's just be cautious about it.
turns.label: Acceptance
